text:
Jordan M: Quick design sync — experimenting with a new card layout for scale policies in the Capacity page. Need quick takes on placement, keyboard/focus order, and copy for the burst control. posting screenshots in figma in a sec :eyes:

Priya K: seeing the mock — 👍 on left-aligned labels. Suggest moving the GPU pool selector into the card header as a small pill; makes it clearer which pool the policy applies to. For tab order: Min -> Max -> Burst -> Pool -> SLO slider -> Save. Keep it linear for keyboard users.

Lee S: Accessibility nits: current blue for the selected chip is #3b82f6 which is 3.4:1 on white — needs >=4.5:1 for normal text. Can we swap to #1e40af or add a 1px darker border to meet contrast? Also ensure focus ring is visible (2px solid focal color) and target hit areas >=44px.

Anika R: Copy tweaks: instead of "Burst capacity" try "Burst (short-term boost)" — helps set expectation. For guardrail copy under Min/Max: "Recommended range: 2–50. Setting min above 10 may increase cost." And an inline helper: "Guardrails prevent destabilizing scaling events." Keep it short.

Priya K: Also propose a subtle affordance for the slider value input: allow keyboard arrows to step by 1 and shift+arrows by 5. For mobile it should still accept direct numeric input.

Jordan M: good call on focus order. For the GPU pool pill, worried about discoverability when multiple policies shown — maybe show pool icon + truncated name and expand on hover. Thoughts on overflow behavior?

Lee S: overflow: show ellipsis + tooltip on hover, but ensure tooltip is accessible via keyboard (aria-describedby tied to focus). Tooltip text should be plain language: "GPU pool: V100-xlarge — 8 GPUs."

AccessibilityBot: quick auto-check: "Contrast fail for .chip.selected (#3b82f6 on #ffffff) — ratio 3.38:1. Suggest #1f3bb3 or increase weight/outline."

DesignBot: uploaded figma frame: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxxx/autoscale-card-v3 (mock contains two variants: header-pill pool + inline-pool). Variant B moves pool into header and compresses description.

Anika R: UX concern — when Burst is enabled, how do we show temporary usage vs baseline? Suggest microcopy under burst: "Burst: temporarily allows extra capacity for up to 5 minutes" and a small clock icon. Also a tooltip: "Burst consumes reserved credits when available."

Priya K: guardrail language idea: use active voice and avoid alarmist tone. Example: "Lowering Min below 2 can increase cold-start latency for infrequent traffic." No "you will" or "danger" language.

Jordan M: Regarding SLO slider — do we show exact percentage or buckets? Current thought: show exact % (e.g., 99.5%) with tick marks at common thresholds (99, 99.5, 99.9). But keyboard users need labelled increments — aria-valuetext should be "SLO: 99.5 percent".

Lee S: confirm: slider needs aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, aria-valuenow, plus aria-label and aria-valuetext. Also have a separate text input that syncs with slider to allow precise edits. For screen readers, announce guardrail tips when value changes beyond recommended range.

DesignBot: small layout question — does the Save CTA live on the card or sticky bottom? Card-level save is clearer when users edit single policy; for bulk edits sticky bottom makes sense. Maybe show contextual Save and a global sticky bar when multiple cards edited.

Anika R: copy for CTA: prefer "Apply changes" over "Save" in this flow — feels a bit more explicit when policy affects capacity and cost.

Jordan M: actionable list: (1) Priya — implement header-pill variant in figma + overflow tooltip, (2) Lee — propose accessible color tokens & focus styles, (3) Anika — final copy suggestions for burst/guardrails and CTA, (4) DesignBot — produce prototype with keyboard nav and tooltip keyboard access. I'll iterate and ping tomorrow morning. Thanks all :sparkles:
